### 📓 Docs Drift Check
**2** anchor(s) derived from **1** changed package(s); no hand-written page names any of them, so this run has **nothing to list** — **not a clean bill of health**. This check sees only pages that NAME a derived anchor: one that documents this change in prose, or enumerates it in an authoring dialect, names none and stays invisible to it on every run.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **10** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 2797f81db7f78d0197f007b7ba502b5816e518c1` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `06cacce13b5a2ff1292d24f2722a07d23ee0c195` — the merge of head `a785894002a5362576dce88bfac41ceaad4a767a` into base `2797f81db7f78d0197f007b7ba502b5816e518c1`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 06cacce13b5a2ff1292d24f2722a07d23ee0c195 && git checkout 06cacce13b5a2ff1292d24f2722a07d23ee0c195
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 2797f81db7f78d0197f007b7ba502b5816e518c1 a785894002a5362576dce88bfac41ceaad4a767a && git checkout -B drift-repro 2797f81db7f78d0197f007b7ba502b5816e518c1 && git merge --no-ff a785894002a5362576dce88bfac41ceaad4a767a

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 2797f81db7f78d0197f007b7ba502b5816e518c1
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `333edb086831ca104cb791040018ee46a5ba7809`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-meta-list-reads.ts, packages/objectql/src/package-scoped-exact-qualifier.test.ts, packages/rest/src/meta-disabled-package-doors.test.ts, .changeset/32354-list-doors-disabled-holder.md + packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-exact-qualifier.ts (disabledExactAddressHolder, read), @objectstack/metadata-core packageDependencyClosure (read)

Face: narrowing (`Clause-②: no (narrowing)` on the changeset), with no `hits`; the whole non-prose diff is in scope. Diff read against merge base `87330e89`.

### ① Derived judgments

- `disabledHolderListing` returns `undefined`, so no list moves, unless the registry can answer and some package is disabled. When it acts, it filters after `isItemOfDisabledPackage` on the effective and execution lists only. `keepDisabledPackages` (the package export) and `type: package` are untouched.
- Scoped list (`'address'`): a name is dropped exactly when `disabledExactAddressHolder` withholds it at that package, the same predicate as the exact read. So `?package=A` and `?package=A.custom` agree with their 404s, and `?package=DEP` keeps its addition (DEP is neither disabled nor a pair).
- Unscoped list (`'unscoped'`): an item is dropped when its own bound package's address is withheld (a disabled holder's pair row), or, for a bundle type, when its package is an addition-only holder whose every base in its declared dependency closure is disabled. Holders are read with `includeDisabledPackages`, so a disable never promotes an addition to a holder. Items with no binding are kept. Answers are memoised per call.
- Pins: the objectql cases × both registration orders × row saved first or last, with a nothing-disabled CONTROL and the pair's own item of a name A ships nothing of (kept). REST covers the pair's row in four orders, the dependent's addition, and the send naming no package, each with a re-enable CONTROL.
- CI on this head was still running at review time (12 success, 16 skipped, 20 in progress, none failed). Landing needs all checks green, and the head will move when #33383 lands (shared test files), which needs a delta record.

### ② Semver level

`Clause-②: no (narrowing)`, the same arm as #33383 for the by-name read and the right one: nothing an author writes or a caller sends is newly accepted, and lists answer less. (The hand-off message said `yes (narrowing)`; the committed changeset says `no (narrowing)`, which governs.) `Metadata-protocol: none`, for the same reason ruled on #33383 (record 6882490650). `@objectstack/metadata-protocol` is `patch` with the BREAKING banner.

### ③ Boundary flags

- No published schema, no governed path. The PR is authored by `objectstack-fleet[bot]` on the relay.
- N1 (nit, consistency): the ADR-0087 disposition here is `not-required (no-migration-prescription)`, while #33383, the by-name half of the same D3 rule, registered semantic entry `disabled-holder-pair-row-bare-read-withheld`. Both pass the gate. An operator reading the upgrade guide sees the read move but not the list move. Registering a sibling entry, or widening #33383's entry `surface` to name the lists, would keep the guide whole.
- N2 (nit, declared regression): while A is disabled, a send made from DEP itself no longer finds DEP's own `fr-FR`, because that send reads the unscoped list. It is declared in the changeset and restored by #32670 (the send door judging served holders). It does not block, since the rule is the epic's and the BREAKING text names it. #32670 should land soon after this.
- This PR also covers the residual N1 of record 6882490650 (#33383: the bare list listing the pair row with every holder disabled).

### ④ Design judgment

The narrowing, judged against the published spec and ADR-0150 D3 on `main`: a disabled package holds no name, and the by-name doors already withhold what it carries. The lists serving it depended on registration and save order, which contradicted the exact reads. This PR makes the list doors use the exact read's own predicate, so it makes the spec's refusal real rather than taking away a declared capability. The dependent's own address still serves its addition, so nothing a dependent ships becomes unreachable. No must-fix or should-fix; N1–N2 are nits. This is the final round.

Delta of record 6882605735 (PASS on `333edb086831ca104cb791040018ee46a5ba7809`). This head merges `main` at `2797f81d`, which carries #33383, and resolves one conflict. Per the pilot rule, only the resolution is reviewed.

### ① Derived judgments

- Parents: `333edb08` (the reviewed head) and `2797f81d` (main). `git merge-tree --write-tree` of the two parents conflicts only in `package-scoped-exact-qualifier.test.ts`, and the merge commit's tree differs from that result in that one file alone.
- Outside that file, the PR's diff against its new base has the same `git patch-id --stable` (`a8202a0f506f`) as the reviewed diff. That includes `protocol-meta-list-reads.ts`, `meta-disabled-package-doors.test.ts` (auto-merged) and the changeset.
- In the conflicted file, main's side is kept whole: the diff from `2797f81d` to this head removes zero lines, so #33383's `[#32814]` block is intact. The PR's `[#32354]` block is added byte-identical to the reviewed head, except that one blank separator line sits before the block instead of after it. No assertion, case or fixture changed.
- Interaction with #33383, read: #33383 changed only the by-name read face (`protocol-meta-item-face.ts`, `isHoldersPairRow`). This PR changes only the list filter. They share no function, and both route the disabled-holder judgment through `disabledOnlyHolderOf` / `disabledExactAddressHolder`, so neither can loosen the other.
- CI on this head was running at review time (4 success, 16 skipped, 20 queued or in progress, none failed). Test Core on this head is the measure for both describe blocks together. The author's local run used a stale `metadata-protocol` dist built before #33383. Landing waits for all checks green.

### ② Semver level

Unchanged from record 6882605735: `Clause-②: no (narrowing)`, `Metadata-protocol: none`, `patch`, `adr-0087: not-required`.

### ③ Boundary flags

Unchanged. N1–N2 of record 6882605735 stand as nits.

### ④ Design judgment

Unchanged. The PR's own source hunks are byte-identical by patch id, and the resolution only places two independent test blocks side by side. Record 6882605735's judgment carries to this head.
